title: Levothyroxine use and bone loss: longitudinal analysis among euthyroid men and women from the Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging
authors: Ghotbi E, McGready J, Hadidchi R, Ibad HA, Simonsick EM, Xue QL, et al.
population: Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging participants euthyroid at all visits who either consistently used or never used levothyroxine; propensity-matched 1:3 within sex (31 male and 53 female users); bone mineral density by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry
funder: Statement in the PubMed record: This research was supported [in part] by the Intramural Research Program of the National Institutes of Health (NIH); 01 AR079620/AR/NIAMS NIH HHS/United States (grant PI Dr Shadpour Demehri). No additional COI to report. The publisher's full text returned a captcha to automated access, so the complete funding statement was not read.
result: In men annual bone mineral density change did not differ between levothyroxine users and non-users in any age stratum. In women, users lost bone mineral density faster than non-users below age 60 (difference -0.010 g/cm2 per year, 95% CI -0.015 to -0.006) and at age 70 to 79 (-0.003, -0.005 to -0.001), despite thyroid function within the reference range at all visits. Results read from the PubMed record; the publisher's full text was not accessible.
